name: Alice's Sister
temperament: A calm, bookish teenager standing on the threshold of adulthood. She is absorbed in her reading, gentle with Alice, and firm about household time. She is also inwardly dreamy: she can half-believe in Wonderland while knowing it is 'dull reality'.

traits.description: Reads an 'adult' book with no pictures and doesn't entertain her little sister. She is content in her own quiet.

evidence.quote: once or twice she had peeped into the book her sister was reading, but it had no pictures or conversations in it
evidence.note: She is already reading like a grown-up, which is exactly what bores Alice.

traits.description: Lets the sleeping Alice rest in her lap, brushes the leaves off her face and wakes her with an endearment and a kiss.

evidence.quote: who was gently brushing away some dead leaves that had fluttered down from the trees upon her face
evidence.note: Her gentle touch is the real-world version of the flying cards.
Listens to the whole dream before sending her in.

traits.trait: Gently authoritative, keeper of household time
traits.description: She is the nearest grown-up voice. She listens, then sends Alice in to tea because it is getting late: kind authority, not bluster.

evidence.quote: but now run in to your tea; it’s getting late
evidence.note: The waking echo of the Rabbit's 'late' and the stuck tea-time.

traits.description: Drifts into her own half-dream of Wonderland, yet knows exactly which farm sounds each fancy comes from. She holds wonder and reality together.

evidence.quote: leaning her head on her hand, watching the setting sun

traits.description: Imagines Alice grown up and hopes she keeps her child's heart, which shows she feels her own childhood ending.

motivation.core: To keep a little of childhood's wonder alive, in Alice and in herself, while taking on the duties of a young woman of the house.
motivation.want: Quiet time to read and think; Alice safe and on time for tea; Alice to grow up without losing her 'simple and loving heart'.
motivation.fear: That growing up means exchanging wonder for 'dull reality'. The source only hints at this.

evidence.note: What she knows waits when she opens her eyes.

motivation.reason: The source gives her no stated motive. The core is drawn from her reverie (ch012-p67-p71) and from her position in the household (world.json frame.social_class: 'an older sister free to read on a weekday afternoon'; mid-teens per ruling 5.6 A).

shifts.from: reading her own book, detached from Alice's childish world
shifts.to: entering that world in her own half-dream and wishing it for Alice's future

habits.habit: Reads with full absorption and doesn't look up when Alice fidgets
Rests her head on her hand when thinking
Uses soft endearments ('Alice dear', 'dear') even when giving an instruction
At the trial (dream glimpse): stands still and silent among the spectators, watching Alice, never taking part
habits.reason: The trial glimpse is a designed staging beat realising H1 ruling 5.3 B (index.json doubling). Her stillness there is designed to match her waking calm.

decision_pattern: Unhurried and observant. She lets things take their course (Alice's nap, Alice's story) and steps in only when it matters (time for tea). She chooses kindness over correction.

taboos.taboo: Never scolds, mocks or dismisses Alice's dream
taboos.rationale: She listens to all of it and says 'It _was_ a curious dream, dear, certainly'. She stands in deliberate contrast to the dream's bullying adults.
taboos.qa_check: No sharp or sarcastic line from her in the wake-up scene.

taboos.taboo: Never uses force or raised-voice authority
taboos.rationale: Her only authority is gentle (she brushes, kisses and reminds). She is the adult model the dream's Queen is not.
taboos.qa_check: Blocking must not show her shaking or pulling Alice awake.

taboos.taboo: At the trial glimpse: never speaks, intervenes or rescues Alice
taboos.rationale: The glimpse is a light echo only (ruling 5.3 B). If she acted, the dream would be resolved by an adult, when Alice must resolve it herself.
taboos.reason: A designed constraint that protects arc-alice-authority.
taboos.qa_check: The sister has no dialogue in ch011-ch012 dream scenes.

facade.note: No disguise. Her detached reading at the start and her tender reverie at the end are the same person seen first from Alice's bored point of view and then from her own.

waking_life_embodiment.summary: She is a waking-world person. In Alice's life she is the nearest and kindest 'grown-up': the one authority figure who listens. In the dream she is only glimpsed as a silent face at the trial (H1 5.3 B), the steady real presence behind the chaos, just before the cards turn to leaves in her hand.
waking_life_embodiment.reason: The trial glimpse is designed (index.json CHAR-alice-sister doubling, ruling 5.3 B). Reading her as the benign counterpart to the dream's adult tyrants is a design interpretation for the coming-of-age frame.

performance_keynote: Quiet, composed and warm. Most of her acting is in her eyes and hands (turning pages, brushing leaves, resting her head on her hand). A faint smile of adult amusement mixed with a little longing.
reason: The source gives her only two scenes and no stated inner life beyond the ch012 reverie. Her motive, fear and trial-glimpse behaviour are designed from that reverie, her household role and H1 ruling 5.3 B.
